nextStoryContext: ensureWorkerContainer (src/supervisor/ensure-container.ts) now imports applyContainerAuthCheck + ContainerAuthError from container-auth.ts (US-002) and gains applyAuthCheckIfPresent(containerName, authCheckSpawnFn): a complete no-op when authCheckSpawnFn is undefined, otherwise it runs the probe and throws ContainerAuthError on loggedIn!==true. It is called UNCONDITIONALLY, immediately after applyConfigIfPresent and immediately before the final `return { action }` -- so even the running->reused branch (which makes zero docker reconcile calls) still runs the auth probe. EnsureWorkerContainerOptions gained an optional authCheckSpawnFn: AuthCheckSpawnFn field (doc comment mirrors configSpawnFn's). makeProductionEnsureContainerFn wires a new authCheckSpawnFn closure (spawnSync-backed, stderr-capturing, same shape as firewallSpawnFn/configSpawnFn/toolchainExecFn -- kept as an independent closure per the seam-independence convention) and threads it into the ensureWorkerContainer call alongside the existing spawnFn/probe/statFn/firewallSpawnFn/configSpawnFn/toolchainExecFn. Test coverage added: auth check fires on all 4 reconcile branches (reused/started/created/rebuilt), fires AFTER config (ordering assertion via a shared order[] array), is a no-op when authCheckSpawnFn is absent, throws ContainerAuthError on loggedIn:false / non-zero exit, and the reused-branch-with-lost-token case explicitly asserts zero spawn.calls while still throwing (proving the reused branch cannot silently dispatch). No new patterns.md bullet was needed: this story is a direct repeat of the already-documented 'configSpawnFn seam + applyConfigIfPresent extraction pattern (US-003, CAM-185, 2026-07-04)' bullet at patterns.md:390, which already generalizes to any new apply*IfPresent seam including this one. The container-auth wiring epic (CAM-241) may have further stories consuming ContainerAuthError at the sidecar-boot call site (e.g. writing a stall-reason marker like 'container-auth-unavailable', already registered by US-001 in sidecar-stalled.ts) or a per-cycle dispatch guard mirroring ToolchainMismatchError's handling in runSidecar/runSupervisor -- check prd.json for the next story's acceptance criteria before assuming scope.
